profile.coi_statement: The authors of this review developed EasyMultiProfiler (Liu B et al., Sci China Life Sci 2025). It is assessed with the same criteria as every other tool, and each statement about it is referenced to its published description.

featured.emphasis: the authors' R workflow for multi-omics integration in microbiome research (Sci China Life Sci 2025), built on SummarizedExperiment / MultiAssayExperiment with extraction, preparation, support, analysis and visualisation modules in a natural-language-style pipeline
featured.name: EasyMultiProfiler (EMP)

profile.outline_guidance: Introduction (why multi-omics integration needs dedicated software); a taxonomy of integration strategies (early / intermediate / late, unsupervised / supervised); general-purpose integration frameworks; microbiome-centred multi-omics tools; web servers and point-and-click platforms; data structures, workflow systems and reproducibility; benchmarking evidence and evaluation criteria; EasyMultiProfiler — design, strengths and limitations relative to the alternatives; a dedicated 'Critical perspectives and controversies' section; recommendations for users and developers and a roadmap; conclusions
profile.query_guidance: integration frameworks (matrix factorisation, multivariate, network, Bayesian, deep learning), R/Bioconductor packages and data structures, microbiome-centred workflows, web servers and point-and-click platforms, benchmarking and comparison studies, reproducibility and workflow standardisation, visualisation, applications in host–microbiome research

reviewers.desc: Peer reviewer, computational biologist who develops omics software. Judge the technical accuracy of how each tool and integration method is described, the evaluation criteria (scalability, data structures, interoperability, documentation, maintenance, reproducibility), and missing key tools.
reviewers.label: Reviewer 1 — bioinformatics methods & software engineering

reviewers.desc: Peer reviewer, microbiome and host-physiology scientist who uses these tools. Judge practical usability, suitability for real study designs (sample coverage, heterogeneous formats), biological interpretability and whether recommendations are actionable.
reviewers.label: Reviewer 2 — microbiome & host–microbe biology (end user)

reviewers.desc: Handling editor. Check that every citation supports its sentence (against the evidence cards), that the comparison is balanced and uses the same criteria for every tool, that the featured workflow is not over-promoted, structure, clarity and English.
reviewers.label: Reviewer 3 — editor, citation integrity & balance

profile.screen_rubric: relevance 3 = describes, benchmarks or directly compares a multi-omics analysis or integration software tool, package, workflow or platform; 2 = a single-omics analysis tool routinely used inside multi-omics workflows, or a methods paper on integration strategies; 1 = context only (reviews of the field, applications); 0 = irrelevant

columns.hint: tool name and type, e.g. 'mixOmics (R package)'
columns.label: Tool (type)

table.select: the most important software tools, packages, workflows or platforms (one row per tool)
table.title: Table 1. Multi-omics analysis software compared
